reasoning: The package follows standard AUR binary packaging practices. It downloads prebuilt binaries from the official upstream GitHub repository (can1357/oh-my-pi) with pinned SHA-256 checksums, which closes the swap risk. The PKGBUILD contains no injection patterns: no executing fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts, and all executable code is confined to functions that are not invoked during metadata extraction. The only disagreement was caused by a tool error in one model, not a genuine security concern.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model failed to review the PKGBUILD due to an HTTP 400 API error, resulting in an 'inconclusive' verdict. This is a tool error, not a security disagreement. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The openrouter report (advisory only) also found it safe, noting a potential hygiene issue with checksum length (63 vs 64 characters) but correctly dismissing it as not grounds for unsafe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD due to HTTP 400 API error
learnings: Handle API failures gracefully by retrying or falling back to a different model instead of marking the entire audit as inconclusive
Distinguish between tool errors and genuine security findings when determining the overall verdict - a tool error should not block a verdict if other models successfully reviewed the same files
Models should not flag checksum length discrepancies as security concerns when they are clearly hygiene issues with no malicious intent
